Overall, our experience was excellent. The decoration, management, and arrangements were very well organized. Thank you, Kohinoor Hall and Mr. Nitin, for making our day memorable.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Nachane
featured_reviews.review_text:
Emptiness. Peace. Once a raucous meeting place of the youth of Hindu colony, now empty of motion and sound. Once venue to a wedding every night, now a barren concrete square. The weddings drove out the playful youth, the pandemic drove away the weddings. Once a flourishing gym, day care, and snack outlet and badminton court, now a mere empty shell.

But like the seeds of grass rising in the concrete topsoil, there remains hope. On Sunday a group of boys and young men set up a wicket and played cricket. They played badly, it is true, but they played.

Maybe there is hope for Bhagini Samaj after all.

Update: one year on, another Sunday. Another group of players. Loud. Hatted. Old young. The bats in their hands reflect the firmer trunks of their youth. The tennis ball a sad ode to when they couldn't afford a second ball if they lost the first; now they don't think before buying one but the strength and eyesight to cart a ball into the first gully has long since left them.

But they still come. In their loud determination ate the calls of re-emergence. Of a time that was and could be again.

Bhagini Samaj lives. Bhagini Samaj will live. Bhagini Samaj must live.

It looks that the place is always booked as you can see decorators either setting up a venue or taking it down. The hall is very spacious. It has a lift but it is down with maintenance. It does have a great open space downstairs which can be used for occasions. Mayur Caterers serve you delicious vegetarian and Jain dishes. The cleanliness aspect ratio is very high. The ceilings are very classy. There is a beautiful swing with a beautiful  green floral background. Amazing vibes can be felt there as it is close to the beach and that too in a centrally located place like Dadar.
